principle: Quality is measured independently from speed and must remain a hard gate where correctness, safety, or usability is essential.

dimensions.correctness: Factual, logical, computational, or task-specific accuracy against the benchmark rubric.
dimensions.completeness: Whether required parts of the task are fulfilled without silently dropping constraints.
dimensions.instruction_fidelity: Whether the result follows explicit user and benchmark requirements.
dimensions.relevance: Whether the result focuses on the actual objective without unnecessary work.
dimensions.consistency: Whether equivalent inputs and repeated runs produce appropriately stable results.
dimensions.robustness: Performance across supported variations, edge cases, malformed inputs, and reasonable adversarial cases.
dimensions.clarity: Whether the output is understandable and actionable for its intended audience.
dimensions.usability: Whether a real user can successfully use the result with reasonable effort.
dimensions.maintainability: Whether generated code/configuration remains understandable, testable, and maintainable where applicable.
dimensions.safety: Whether the result respects applicable safety, privacy, authorization, and policy constraints.
dimensions.verification_quality: Whether important claims or actions are appropriately checked before being presented as reliable.
dimensions.calibration: Whether confidence and uncertainty appropriately track observed correctness.
dimensions.reproducibility: Whether the measured quality can be reproduced under the documented environment and fixture conditions.
dimensions.human_preference: Human-rated usefulness or preference when objective scoring is insufficient, using documented evaluation protocols.
dimensions.regression_resilience: Whether improvements preserve previously passing behavior.

evaluation_rules.separate_scores: Report each applicable quality dimension separately before calculating any aggregate.
evaluation_rules.hard_gates: Correctness, safety, and required instruction fidelity cannot be compensated for by speed, cost, or style improvements.
evaluation_rules.evidence: Human preference, automated judges, and model-based evaluators must be labeled by evaluator type and should be calibrated against independent evidence where practical.
evaluation_rules.anti_gaming: Benchmark fixtures, rubrics, hidden tests, and acceptance criteria must not be weakened solely to improve Buddy's score.
evaluation_rules.mastery: A benchmark requires its defined quality gates plus applicable performance, reliability, and regression requirements before mastery can be claimed.

quality_performance_tradeoff: Track quality and efficiency as separate dimensions and publish the Pareto frontier where enough measurements exist. Never collapse a serious quality regression into an apparently positive composite score.
public_pages: Expose quality dimensions, performance dimensions, evaluator type, sample size, confidence/uncertainty where available, trend, and benchmark state.
